name: Hohe Salve
kurzbeschreibung: The Hohe Salve at 1,828 m above sea level in the Kitzbühel Alps: Tyrol's most beautiful panoramic mountain with the Salvenkirchlein chapel, a revolving panoramic terrace, and views of 70 three-thousanders.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Hohe Salve is a striking, freestanding pyramid-shaped mountain at an altitude of 1,828 meters in the Kitzbühel Alps in Tyrol's Unterland region. Located between the Brixental, Söllandl, and Inntal valleys, the mountain peak is reverently referred to by locals as the “Rigi of Tyrol.” Thanks to its exposed, solitary position, the Hohe Salve offers one of the most overwhelming 360-degree summit panoramas in the entire Central European region: the distant view extends over more than 70 snow-capped three-thousanders – from the Großglockner and Großvenediger across the Zillertal Alps to the rugged limestone cliffs of the Wilder Kaiser and the Bavarian Prealps.

Route & Requirements

The mountain's history as a sacred cult site dates back to pre-Christian times. At its highest point stands the world-famous Salvenkirchlein (officially consecrated to Saint John the Baptist): first documented in 1589, this whitewashed church with its onion dome is Austria's highest pilgrimage church. For centuries, farmers and believers have made pilgrimages to the Salve on its patron saint's day to ask for blessings for the weather and abundant harvests. Inside, a Baroque altar and a life-sized statue of the patron saint impress visitors.

Visit & Arrival

The Hohe Salve is accessible daily from 08:30 to 17:00 during summer (late May to late October) and winter (December to April) with modern cable cars. Summer mountain railway prices (as of season 2025/2026): Ascent and descent adults approx. €33.50, youth approx. €25.00, children (born 2009–2018) approx. €17.00; toddlers ride free. Access to the summit plateau, the Salvenkirchlein, and the sundial path is included free of charge with the mountain railway ticket. Holders of the Kitzbüheler Alpen Summer Card or the SkiWelt Erlebnis-Wanderpass ride for free. Arrival by cable car: Choose between the modern gondola lifts from Hopfgarten im Brixental or Söll directly to the summit station. Arrival by train: ÖBB train station Hopfgarten Berglift is only about 150 meters from the valley station. By car: Via the B178 or B170 to Hopfgarten or Söll to the large free mountain railway car parks.

Tips

The gondola lifts from Hopfgarten and Söll to the summit, as well as the revolving panoramic terrace, are exemplarily barrier-free and wheelchair-accessible; the circular path around the summit plateau is also flat and suitable for strollers. Plan lunch on the rotating panoramic terrace and try original Tyrolean Germknödel or Kaiserschmarrn with a view of the Großglockner.
preis: Gondola ascent and descent approx. €33.50; Salvenkirchlein & sundial path free
oeffnungszeiten: Summer season late May to late Oct daily 08:30–17:00 (lift operation)
